text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Ramussen foresees a probable fresh Danish referendum next year on Europe after the IGC intergovernmental conference reforms of the workings of the union in summer 1997.

--- Only nine days before Denmark, Norway and Sweden are due to sign the European Union's Schengen open frontier agreement, the People's Party (a small right-wing grouping) is demanding that a national referendum be called on the issue while left-wing parties are accusing the government of surrendering Danish sovereignty and endangering the Nordic passport union.
--- Changes in future European Union agricultural subsidies could mean that Denmark will become a net contributor to the union in 1997.

--- Danish police have rejected criticism of their decision to issue in February a new Danish passport using a reproduction from a 1,000-year-old runestone showing Jesus Christ on the crucifix on the inside cover. The foreign ministry and embassies fear that the use of a Christ symbol in the new passport might cause Danish citizens problems in Islamic countries.

--- A new double taxation agreement between Denmark and Germany to be introduced on January 1, 1997 makes it very attractive for German old age pensioners to move to Denmark. This combined with low housing prices in southern Jutland, north of the German border, could spark a major influx of German old age pensioners into Denmark.
